references.text: Jacob's blessing over Judah speaks of the scepter (שֵׁבֶט) not departing from Judah, linking to the prophecy of a ruler rising from Israel.
Isaiah prophesies about a shoot from the stump of Jesse, a messianic prophecy describing the coming ruler from David's line.
Nations shall walk to the light of Israel, a parallel to the star that rises from Jacob.
Jeremiah prophesies about a righteous Branch for David, who will reign as king—a messianic parallel.
Amos speaks of raising up the fallen hut of David, connected to the promise of a ruler rising from Israel.
Micah prophesies about a ruler from Bethlehem who will shepherd Israel, a clear messianic prophecy.
The wise men from the East saw his star and came to worship the newborn king of the Jews—a direct fulfillment of the star from Jacob.
The star led the wise men to the place where Jesus was, confirming the connection between Balaam's prophecy and the birth of the Messiah.
Zechariah sings about the sunrise from on high who will visit us, a light-themed parallel to the rising star.
Peter refers to the prophetic word as a lamp and the morning star that rises, with a possible allusion to Balaam's prophecy.
Jesus calls himself the Root and Offspring of David, the bright Morning Star—a direct fulfillment of the prophecy about the star from Jacob.
